# Apple site and app: final design spec ("Ember Rail" with a Baseplate toy)

## 0. What was measured and what was not

**Measured by me**
- I recomputed all colour ratios below with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula. They match the Ember Rail values for the 5 surfaces in both themes. The brick edge values are also computed.
- I rendered the final lockup on the dark and light grounds at 640px wide, and a 16px favicon tile, with `qlmanage`. The lockup reads correctly in both themes. At 16px only the brick silhouette and studs resolve, not the chevron.

**Not measured**
- No repo test, build or Lighthouse run. Lighthouse is not installed (`which lighthouse` found nothing).
- No keyboard or screen-reader pass.
- No JS or CSS byte sizes. The 24,451 B inline-JS figure, the 36,000 B budget and the 18,114 B markup+CSS figure come from the direction authors' notes and are unverified.
- The two lighter favicon variants were not rendered. The light-mode logo was rendered only as a lockup.

**Gaps in the brief**
- No "design checklist" exists in the repo. §11 below is authored fresh.
- Lighthouse scope is undefined. I assume all four categories, mobile profile, every route.
- Claude Design / DesignSync is blocked until the owner runs `/design-login`. This spec was authored by hand.

## 1. Scorecard

Scores are my judgement from reading the three briefs, 0 to 10. They are not measurements.

| Direction | Originality / memorability | Fit: young Roblox creators and paid-tool credibility | Accessibility | Perf cost of motion and gimmick (10 = cheapest) | Implementable across both apps | Total /50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stud & Plate | 8 | 7 (youth 8, credibility 6) | 7 | 7 | 6 | 35 |
| **Ember Rail** | 6 | 8 (youth 6, credibility 9) | 9 | 9 | 8 | **40** |
| Front Page | 9 | 5 (youth 7, credibility 5) | 6 | 8 | 4 | 32 |

Reasons for each score:
- **Stud & Plate**
  - It is the most appealing to kids.
  - Amber fails as light-mode text (1.63:1), so it is a fill-only trap.
  - The 14x6 grid with 44px targets does not fit a 375px phone as drafted.
  - The flat-plate edge on every surface means restyling all of the app.
  - Studs risk the V3 line "not an in-game studded HUD" if overused.
- **Ember Rail**
  - It is the only direction with no V3 tension. It is restrained, near-black and dark by default.
  - Its Rail is real run state, so it fits the "no synthetic activity" rule.
  - It has the strongest contrast margins: control borders reach 3:1 on all five surfaces.
  - Its weakness is originality for a young audience. Its logo also had a leaf-topped brick that could be read as resembling Apple Inc.'s mark.
- **Front Page**
  - It is the most memorable.
  - It needs an owner exception to the `check-copy` 56px display cap, which is a hard guard.
  - It adds a serif face with uneven metrics, and light-mode flare text has only 4.51:1 headroom.
  - It reads as louder than V3's "restrained", and it touches the most tests.

**Winner: Ember Rail.**

**Grafts**
- From Stud & Plate:
  - the Baseplate toy as the landing gimmick, with the "Describe this to Apple" bridge;
  - stud-shaped status LED and loader;
  - the "missing brick" 404;
  - the 2px solid plate edge on the primary button and the bricks only;
  - the brick-hue decoration rule.
- From Front Page:
  - "Try an example" chips that fill the textarea on click (real buttons, no auto-typing);
  - numbered mono section labels such as `01`;
  - the permanent "illustration" label discipline;
  - `content-visibility: auto` on below-fold sections.
- Logo fix: the leaf is replaced by two studs and the mark gains a prompt cut-out. This removes the fruit-leaf reading.

**Rejected**
- A webfont.
- Serif display and poster-scale type.
- ui-rounded as the primary face.
- Aurora, glass and gradients.
- Any ambient looping canvas.

## 2. Principles

1. **Instrument, not toy-box.** Dark, flat, hairline-bordered. One signal colour (Ember). It marks the primary action, the active or live step, and the focus ring.
2. **The Rail is the structure.** A 1px line with square nodes. On the site the nodes are page sections. In the app they are the real run steps.
3. **Snap.** Radii are tight, layout lands on a 4px unit, and motion is short and precise. A small spring is used only for "click" moments.
4. **Everything shown is real.** Illustrations are labelled. Any playful element reacts to real input or real state only.
5. **The stud motif is capped at 3 appearances per screen.** The allowed ones are the logo, the Baseplate toy, and the status LED or loader.
6. **Both apps share one token sheet.** `apps/site/src/styles/apple-minimal.css` and `apps/web/src/design/apple-minimal.css` carry identical values, and the same-product test is kept and re-pointed.
7. **RTL-safe, English-only copy.** Logical properties only. Copy stays lower-case after the first word, with no exclamation marks.

## 3. Tokens

Existing bare token names are kept so the contrast tests can keep deriving pairs. Raw hex appears only in the token sheet. `--accent` changes value, so the pins in `living-background.test.mjs` must be deliberately rewritten.

### Dark (default; `:root` and `[data-theme="dark"]`)

```css
--paper:#0a0c10; --paper-2:#0e1116; --surface:#12151b; --surface-2:#181c24; --surface-3:#1f242e;
--ink:#f3f5f8; --ink-2:#c3c9d4; --muted:#9aa3b2; --faint:#8791a1;
--accent:#ff8a4c; --accent-text:#ff8a4c; --on-accent:#1a0d05; --ring:#ff8a4c;
--good:#5fd39a; --warn:#f0c75e; --bad:#ff7d8c;
--danger-fill:#b3261e; --on-danger:#ffffff;
--hairline:#232833; --line:#3a4150; --line-strong:#6b7587;
--accent-soft: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, var(--surface));
--scrim: rgb(0 0 0 / .6);
--theme-color:#0a0c10;
/* bricks: decoration only, never the sole carrier of meaning */
--brick-red:#ff6b57; --brick-blue:#4f8cff; --brick-green:#3fc476; --brick-yellow:#ffc23a;
--brick-red-edge:#733027; --brick-blue-edge:#243f73; --brick-green-edge:#1c5835; --brick-yellow-edge:#73571a;
```

### Light (`[data-theme="light"]`)

```css
--paper:#f7f8fa; --paper-2:#f1f3f6; --surface:#ffffff; --surface-2:#eef0f4; --surface-3:#e6e9ef;
--ink:#0d1017; --ink-2:#3a4150; --muted:#515b6e; --faint:#586275;
--accent:#a63f0a; --accent-text:#a63f0a; --on-accent:#ffffff; --ring:#a63f0a;
--good:#0f6e52; --warn:#7a4f00; --bad:#a81f35;
--danger-fill:#b3261e; --on-danger:#ffffff;
--hairline:#dfe3ea; --line:#c8cdd8; --line-strong:#7c8597;
--scrim: rgb(13 16 23 / .5);
--theme-color:#f7f8fa;
/* brick hues and edges identical to dark */
```

### Measured text contrast

Columns are paper / paper-2 / surface / surface-2 / surface-3. The minimum is 4.5:1.

| Token | Dark | Light |
|---|---|---|
| ink | 17.92 / 17.32 / 16.74 / 15.63 / 14.24 | 17.91 / 17.12 / 19.03 / 16.68 / 15.65 |
| ink-2 | 11.77 / 11.37 / 10.99 / 10.26 / 9.35 | 9.63 / 9.21 / 10.23 / 8.97 / 8.42 |
| muted | 7.69 / 7.43 / 7.19 / 6.71 / 6.12 | 6.43 / 6.15 / 6.84 / 5.99 / 5.62 |
| faint (lowest 4.88 dark, 5.05 light) | 6.15 / 5.94 / 5.74 / 5.36 / 4.88 | 5.78 / 5.53 / 6.14 / 5.38 / 5.05 |
| accent-text | 8.38 / 8.10 / 7.83 / 7.31 / 6.66 | 5.92 / 5.66 / 6.29 / 5.52 / 5.17 |
| good | 10.50 / 10.15 / 9.81 / 9.16 / 8.35 | 5.86 / 5.60 / 6.23 / 5.46 / 5.12 |
| warn | 12.15 / 11.74 / 11.35 / 10.59 / 9.66 | 6.71 / 6.41 / 7.13 / 6.25 / 5.86 |
| bad | 7.98 / 7.71 / 7.45 / 6.96 / 6.34 | 6.79 / 6.49 / 7.21 / 6.32 / 5.93 |
| line-strong (non-text, min 3:1) | 4.21 / 4.07 / 3.93 / 3.67 / 3.35 | 3.49 / 3.34 / 3.71 / 3.25 / 3.05 |

- **Ordering:** ink, ink-2, muted, faint descend in both themes, as `contrast.test.mjs` requires.
- **On-accent text:** 8.15 in dark and 6.29 in light.
- **White on danger fill:** 6.54 for `#b3261e`.
- **Focus ring:** accent against paper is 8.38 in dark and 5.92 in light. Against surface-3 it is 6.66 and 5.17.

### Rules that prevent regressions
- `--hairline` and `--line` are decorative and exempt. They never carry a control boundary. Inputs, the composer, checkboxes and segmented controls use `--line-strong`.
- `faint` is for metadata and placeholders only. A new tint on surface-3 needs a re-check.
- Never put accent text on `--accent-soft`; use `--ink` there.
- Status (good, warn, bad) always travels with an icon and a word. Warn is gold and bad is rose so they stay apart from Ember.
- Brick hues on light paper have edge ratios of 9.06 (red), 9.72 (blue), 7.92 (green) and 6.36 (yellow). On dark paper the edges are 1.9 to 2.9 and the fills are 6.08 to 12.14, so contrast holds in each theme.
  - In light mode every brick must draw its 2px `--brick-*-edge`. The bare fills are 1.52 to 3.03 against paper.
  - Occupied versus empty cells is distinguished by shape (a raised brick against a recessed stud slot), not colour.

## 4. Typography

No webfont and no downloads, so the system stack is the final decision and the font-token tests stay valid.

```css
--font-sans: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", system-ui, Arial, sans-serif;
--font-mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
```

| Role | Size | Line height | Weight | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| display-xl (landing h1 only) | `clamp(2.25rem, 6vw + .5rem, 3.5rem)` | 1.05 | 600 | tracking -0.03em; 3.5rem is the `check-copy` cap |
| display (page h1) | 2.25rem | 1.1 | 600 | -0.02em |
| h2 | 1.75rem | 1.2 | 600 | |
| h3 | 1.25rem | 1.3 | 600 | |
| body-lg | 1.125rem | 1.6 | 400 | landing and docs lead |
| body | 1rem | 1.6 | 400 | app default |
| ui | 0.875rem | 1.45 | 500 | labels, buttons |
| caption | 0.8125rem | 1.4 | 400 | minimum text size |
| mono | 0.8125rem | 1.5 | 400 | tool names, paths, code |
| eyebrow | 0.75rem | 1.3 | 600 | tracking 0.06em, mono, sentence case |

- **Section numbers:** a mono `01` ledger label comes before each landing section eyebrow. It is not all-caps.
- **Weights:** 400 body and 500/600 UI and display, nothing above 600. This supersedes DESIGN-LOCK "nothing above 400". Record that in `docs/DESIGN-TYPE.md`.
- **Numerals:** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on credits, usage, counts and timings.
- **Wrapping:** `text-wrap: balance` on headings and `pretty` on paragraphs. Measure is 64ch for prose and 40ch for hero sub-copy.
- **Input text** is at least 16px so iOS does not zoom.
- **Sizes** are in rem so 200% zoom works. Every rule uses logical properties.
- **The wordmark** is drawn as paths, so it needs no font.

## 5. Spacing, radius, elevation

- **Spacing unit** is 4px. Scale: `--s-1..9` = 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96.
- **Gutters:** 16px at 375px, 24px from 640px, 32px from 1024px.
- **Content widths:** content max 1120px, docs article 720px, chat column 760px.
- **Header heights:** `--nav-h` 56px on the site, 48px for the app top bar.
- **Breakpoints:** 640, 900 (Rail appears), 960, 1280.
- **Radius:** `--r-xs` 4 (chips, badges), `--r-sm` 6 (buttons, inputs), `--r-md` 10 (cards), `--r-lg` 14 (dialogs), `--r-xl` 20 (composer, hero panel, pinned). Fully round only for status dots and avatars.
- **Elevation** comes from surface steps, not shadows:

| Level | Treatment |
|---|---|
| 0 | paper |
| 1 | surface plus 1px `--hairline` (cards) |
| 2 | surface-2 plus 1px `--line-strong` (inputs, composer) |
| 3 | menus, dialogs, popovers: surface-2, 1px `--line`, one soft drop shadow `0 8px 24px rgb(0 0 0 / .35)` in dark or `0 8px 24px rgb(13 16 23 / .12)` in light |

- **Plate edge** is the only graft shadow: `box-shadow: 0 2px 0 <solid darker shade>` with no blur. It is allowed only on the primary button and on bricks. It presses to 0 offset and `translateY(2px)`.
- **Blur** (`backdrop-filter`) is used only on the sticky top bar and the composer, never on repeated list items.
- **No gradients, no glow, no aurora.** `glass.css` is retired.
- **Z-index:** base 0, rail 5, sticky bar 20, drawer 30, dialog 40, toast 50, skip link 60.
- **Touch targets** are at least 44px.
- **Focus ring:** `2px solid var(--ring)` at a 3px offset, on every control, never removed, with no transition. DESIGN-LOCK says a 4px offset; this spec supersedes it for consistency with the Rail geometry.

## 6. Motion

**Principle:** motion shows real state change, or a labelled illustration. Nothing loops by default. Only `transform` and `opacity` animate.

```css
--dur-1:90ms; --dur-2:160ms; --dur-3:260ms; --dur-4:480ms;
--ease-out:cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);
--ease-in-out:cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1);
--ease-snap:linear(0,.55 18%,1.12 42%,.98 62%,1);
```

1. **Press:** buttons go down 2px over 90ms. The plate edge shrinks from 2px to 0. Release uses `--ease-snap`.
2. **Reveal on scroll:** blocks rise 8px and fade in over 260ms, staggered 40ms and capped at 6 items.
   - It reuses the `[data-reveal]` / `.is-in` mechanism.
   - Content is visible without JS and with reduced motion.
   - The 2.6s failsafe and `.no-js` handling stay, as `reveal-cannot-hide-content.test.mjs` demands.
3. **Rail draw (site):** the Rail line is a `scaleY` driven by scroll progress.
   - It uses CSS scroll-driven animation where supported, with an `IntersectionObserver` fallback.
   - Nodes fill as their section crosses 40% of the viewport.
4. **Rail in the app:** a node changes only on a real run event. The active node pulses (opacity 1 to 0.55, 1.4s) only while a run is active. The pulse stops on complete, pause and error.
5. **Run illustration:** in `#inside`, four nodes (Plan, Change in Studio, Check, Done) light up once over about 2.4s and rest on the final state. The label "Illustration" stays on screen. There is no fake output and no numbers.
6. **Baseplate placement:** a brick drops in with `--ease-snap` over 220ms.
7. **Logo Snap:** see §7.
8. **Loader:** three studs light in sequence at 900ms per cycle. It runs only during real loading and stops on completion or error.
9. **Toasts:** drop in 12px with `--ease-snap` and leave with a plain fade.
10. **Page transitions:** `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` with a 160ms fade, declared only inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
11. **Theme toggle:** the two glyphs swap over 140ms. There is no full-page crossfade.
12. **Dialogs and drawers:** 160ms translate and fade.
13. **Off-screen and hidden tabs:** any loop pauses via `IntersectionObserver` and `visibilitychange`.

**Reduced motion** (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and the in-app pref from `lib/prefs.ts`) is off, not shortened:
- `animation: none; transition: none`, with no 0.01ms trick.
- No transforms, no loops, no view transition, no overshoot.
- State changes are instant colour or opacity swaps.
- The Rail is drawn fully filled. The site's progress bar is hidden.
- The loader becomes three static studs plus the word "Loading".
- Baseplate placement is instant.
- The logo stud is simply seated.
- The active Rail node is a static ring.

**Banned:**
- Ambient drift, parallax, aurora and looping canvas.
- `cursor: none`, pointer-following overlays and sound.
- `will-change` except on the Rail node pulse.

## 7. The gimmick

Two parts. Both respond only to real input or real state.

### A. The Baseplate (landing hero)

A small playable building toy under the hero composer, in DOM and SVG only. It uses no canvas, WebGL, three.js or new dependency, and has an estimated 2 to 3 KB gzip of JS.

- **Grid size:** 12 columns by 5 rows from 640px up. 7 columns by 4 rows below 640px, so cells stay at least 44px at 375px. The original 14x6 draft did not fit a phone.
- **Interaction:**
  - Click or tap an empty stud to drop a 1x1 brick.
  - Drag along a row to lay a longer brick.
  - Click a brick to remove it.
  - Stacking is allowed to 3 high.
  - A four-swatch tray picks the colour: red, blue, green, yellow.
  - A "Clear baseplate" button resets it.
- **Keyboard and assistive tech:**
  - `role="grid"` with a roving tabindex.
  - Arrow keys move, Space or Enter places or removes, `1`-`4` choose a colour, Escape returns focus to the page.
  - A polite live region announces "Red brick placed at column 3, row 1".
  - Every cell has a real `aria-label`.
  - A "Skip the baseplate" link precedes the grid. The toy is optional and never the page's main content.
- **Honesty:**
  - Every brick came from a visitor's click or key press. Nothing is pre-built or simulated.
  - The visible caption reads "A toy baseplate. Place bricks with your hands. Apple builds in Studio from words."
  - The toy never pretends to be Apple building a game.
- **Bridge to the real product:**
  - Once at least one brick exists, a "Describe this to Apple" button appears.
  - It fills `textarea.composer-input` with a sentence computed from the real bricks, for example "A small tower, 3 bricks high, red and blue."
  - It never submits. The visitor edits it and sends it with the real send button, which posts to `/app/signup`.
- **Persistence:** the layout may be kept in `sessionStorage`. Nothing is sent anywhere.
- **Guards:**
  - Hover feedback is a CSS `:hover`/`:focus` highlight on the cell. No ghost brick follows the pointer, which keeps `cursor-never-blinds.test.mjs` green.
  - Bricks use the `--brick-*` tokens with their edges (§3).
  - A brick never reuses the Ember accent; yellow is the fourth hue.
- **Echo scale elsewhere:**
  - The app's connection LED is a stud-shaped dot, green only when Studio is really paired.
  - The loader uses three studs.
  - The 404 shows one empty stud slot with the line "one brick missing".

### B. The Snap (logo, tied to real state)

The logo's right-hand stud is a separate shape (`.stud--snap`). It sits lifted (`translateY(-3px) rotate(-8deg)`) and clicks into place with `--ease-snap` over 320ms when something real happens.
- **App:** it snaps when Studio pairing actually completes. It lifts on disconnect (`paused_disconnected`) and snaps again on reconnect plus the explicit Continue (`awaiting_continue`). It is inert before first pairing.
- **Site:** it lifts when focus first enters the hero composer and snaps on submit. On touch there is no hover trigger, so focus and submit are the triggers.
- **Reduced motion:** the stud is simply seated.

### C. The Rail as a reading instrument
It runs down the inline-start margin on long pages as `<nav aria-label="On this page">`.
- Nodes use real section ids, so the `links-resolve` test can check the fragments.
- Below 900px it collapses to a 2px top progress bar.
- Content gets `padding-inline-start: 56px` from 900px up.

**Retired:** the picks canvas kit (`NoiseField`, `ParticleWord`, `BeamFlow`, `Aura`, `PointerRim`). That requires deliberate rewrites of `picks-landing.test.mjs`, `animation-actually-wins.test.mjs` and `phone-drops-layers.test.mjs`, not deletions.

## 8. Logo

**Concept.** A rounded brick with two top studs and a prompt chevron plus cursor cut out of its face. It says "a command inside a Roblox brick". It has no fruit silhouette, no leaf and no bite, to avoid Apple Inc.'s mark. The wordmark "Apple" is monoline rounded strokes, so it needs no font and inverts through `currentColor`.

**Primary lockup**, inline use only because it resolves `var(--accent)`:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 128 36" role="img" aria-label="Apple" fill="none">
  <g fill="var(--accent,#ff8a4c)">
    <path d="M10 11H22A7 7 0 0 1 29 18V26A7 7 0 0 1 22 33H10A7 7 0 0 1 3 26V18A7 7 0 0 1 10 11ZM9.4 16.2 19.6 22 9.4 27.8 7.8 25.2 13.6 22 7.8 18.8ZM21 26.4H25.6A1.2 1.2 0 0 1 25.6 28.8H21A1.2 1.2 0 0 1 21 26.4Z" fill-rule="evenodd"/>
    <rect class="stud" x="7" y="6.5" width="7" height="5.5" rx="2"/>
    <rect class="stud stud--snap" x="18" y="6.5" width="7" height="5.5" rx="2"/>
  </g>
  <g transform="translate(-4 0)" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
    <path d="M44 27 52 9 60 27M47 21H57"/>
    <path d="M69 15V33"/><circle cx="75" cy="21" r="6"/>
    <path d="M89 15V33"/><circle cx="95" cy="21" r="6"/>
    <path d="M109 8V27"/>
    <path d="M116 21H128A6 6 0 1 0 126.2 25.3"/>
  </g>
</svg>
```

```css
.stud--snap{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:50% 100%;transition:transform 320ms var(--ease-snap)}
.mark[data-state="lifted"] .stud--snap{transform:translateY(-3px) rotate(-8deg)}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.stud--snap{transition:none;transform:none!important}}
```

**Usage rules**
- Mark only: `viewBox="0 0 32 36"`, with the wordmark group removed.
- The lockup uses no `id`s (no mask), so it is safe to inline more than once per page.
- Colour:
  - The wordmark uses `color: var(--ink)`.
  - The mark uses `--accent`: `#ff8a4c` in dark and `#a63f0a` in light. The Ember mark on light paper is 5.92:1, and on dark paper 8.38:1.
- Files loaded through `<img>` (favicon, `og.png`, touch icons) cannot read CSS variables. Export baked files from this one source:
  - `logo-dark.svg` (ink `#f3f5f8`, Ember `#ff8a4c`) and `logo-light.svg` (ink `#0d1017`, Ember `#a63f0a`).
  - Favicon: a `#0a0c10` rounded tile (rx 7 on a 32 box) holding the `#ff8a4c` mark scaled 0.8 and offset `translate(3.2 2.4)`.
  - For tiles smaller than 24px, drop the underscore cursor and keep the chevron. I did not render that variant.
- Sizes: the mark alone is for 16px and up. At 16px only the silhouette and studs resolve, which is acceptable for a favicon. The lockup is for 96px wide and up. Clear space is the stud height (5.5 units) on all sides. Do not recolour, outline or stretch it.
- Surfaces to update together:
  - `apps/site/public/favicon.svg`, `apple-touch-icon.png`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`, `og.png`, `site.webmanifest`.
  - `apps/site/brand/apple-mark-source.png` and `og.html` (rewrite self-contained, with no Google Fonts).
  - `AppleMark.astro`, `AppleGlyph` in `apps/web`, the app's data-URI favicon, the app rail and the assistant avatar.
  - The plugin icon (Creator Store asset 107230158271368) is out of scope.
- Open item: the owner should check whether this mark can be misread as resembling a known mark. I did no trademark search.

## 9. Landing page (`/`)

Layout stays the existing Landing layout. Keep these hooks, because tests pin them: `header#site-nav`, `#menu-toggle`, `#primary-nav`, `a.nav__cta`, `a.nav__signin`, `footer.foot`, `.closing`, `section.hero`, `h1#hero-title`, `form.composer`, `textarea.composer-input`, `button.composer-send`. Keep the section ids `#inside`, `#capabilities` and `#models`. Copy is test-pinned: restyle and restructure, and do not invent new claims or numbers.

**0. Chrome**
- Sticky 56px bar with a hairline bottom border. It has blur, and blur only here.
- Inline-start: logo lockup.
- Centre: Product (`/#inside`), Engine (`/models`), Showcase, Pricing, Docs.
- Inline-end: theme toggle, Sign in, Create an account (primary Ember button).
- A skip link comes first.
- Below 900px the Rail becomes a 2px top progress bar.

**1. Hero**
- `h1#hero-title` uses display-xl. It keeps the current copy, which markets prompt-to-complete-game creation and not studded-only games.
- A 40ch sub-line in plain words.
- The real composer is enabled for visitors and posts to `/app/signup`. It is a level-2 `--r-xl` panel with a visible `--line-strong` border. Under it sits the line "Pairs with Roblox Studio through a plugin."
- Below that, "Try an example" chips: three real `<button type="button">` that fill the textarea on click. No auto-typing and no replay.
- Below that, the Baseplate with its caption and bridge (§7A).
- On phones the order is h1, composer, chips, Baseplate.
- The Snap triggers on composer focus and submit.

**2. `#inside`: how a run actually goes**
- Four Rail-linked steps: Plan, Change in Studio, Check, Done. Each has a mono `01`-`04` label, one sentence and a currentColor line icon from the existing set. The sentences are pinned or reused copy.
- The illustration plays once and carries a permanent "Illustration" label. It shows no timings and no counts, because `counted-copy.test.mjs` polices those.
- If a screenshot appears, it keeps its source and date label (`built-screen-is-evidence`, `recorded-run-is-evidence`).

**3. `#capabilities`**
- The three demo stages (`data-demo` tree, eye, code) keep their hooks and script: `rd-*`, `cw-*`, `lu-*`, `stage-tab`, `stage-tabs`, `demo-stage`.
- They are restyled as flat panels with hairline borders and mono labels.
- Tabs scroll horizontally on mobile, and markers stay finger-sized (`demo-stages-fit` test).
- Each carries an "Illustration" label wherever it is not live data.

## 11. Component rules

**Buttons** (44px minimum height, `--r-sm`)
- **Primary:** `--accent` fill, `--on-accent` text, 2px plate edge, press down 2px.
- **Secondary:** surface-2 fill, `--line-strong` border, ink text.
- **Ghost:** no border, ink-2 text, and `--surface-2` on hover.
- **Danger:** `--danger-fill` with `--on-danger`. Used for confirmation only.
- **Stop:** a danger-outline control with its own enabled state.
- **Disabled:** `aria-disabled` plus a faint label, and never colour-only. Visible focus on every variant.

**Inputs**
- 44px tall, 16px text, `--r-sm`, a `--line-strong` 1px border, and a visible label above.
- Placeholder is `--faint` and never replaces a label.
- Errors show an icon, a word and the next step, and are announced once.
- Do not rely on colour alone.

**Cards**
- Level 1: surface plus a hairline, `--r-md`. Interactive cards get a `--line-strong` border on hover and a focus ring.
- No blur.
- A card that is a link has one link target.

**Chat**
- **Assistant:** unboxed text on paper at 16px, with a 1.6 line height.
- **User:** a surface-2 block with a 1px hairline and `--r-md`, aligned to the inline-end.
- **Evidence:** collapsible "Inspect" cards. A mono header carries the tool name and state icon, plus a 2px state rule at inline-start.
- **Code, trees and tables:** on surface-2 with mono type. They are lazy or paginated, and secrets or hidden reasoning are never rendered.
- **Streaming:** one canonical stream, with no duplicated paragraph and no artificial typing replay.

**Status chips**
- An icon, a word and a status colour, square-ish with `--r-xs`. The LED is a stud-shaped dot.

**Dialogs, menus, toasts**

## 12. Design checklist (every page must pass)

This replaces the missing repo checklist. It builds on the existing tests and guards. Each item is pass or fail.

**Brand and content**
1. Product name is Apple. Infrastructure names stay "golem" and are never user-visible.
2. English only. Copy is lower-case after the first word, with no exclamation marks, no "Oops" and no selling. `scripts/check-copy.mjs`, `scripts/check-rebrand.mjs`.
3. No model menu, no Plan/Agent/Autonomous selector, no Apple MAX, Jev or training surfaces.
4. Every illustration, demo or toy is labelled as such. No synthetic activity appears as live. The `proof-is-evidence`, `recorded-run-is-evidence` and `built-screen-is-evidence` guards stay green.
5. No claim of live billing or a public plugin store release.

**Tokens and style**
6. No raw hex outside the token sheet. `apple-minimal.css` is the only token source on each app. The site and app token values match.
7. No gradients, glow, aurora or `backdrop-filter` except on the top bar and composer.
8. Both themes work, and `theme-color` follows the page ground. A pre-paint theme script and toggle are on every layout (`theme-on-every-route`).
9. Text weight is at most 600. The h1 is at most 3.5rem. Minimum text is 0.8125rem.

**Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)**
10. Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 on every surface in both themes (`contrast.test.mjs`). Non-text is at least 3:1 (focus ring, `--line-strong` control borders).
11. Focus: a visible `2px solid var(--ring)` ring at a 3px offset on every control. It is never removed.
12. Information is never carried by colour alone. Status always has an icon and a word.
13. One `main`, a heading hierarchy that does not skip, and correct landmarks (`scripts/check-site-semantics.mjs`).
14. A skip link, a full keyboard path, and focus trapped and restored in dialogs and drawers.
15. Touch targets are at least 44px.
16. Zoom to 200% works with no loss, and there is no horizontal scroll at 375px with a 16px gutter. The page also works from 320px.
17. Reduced motion turns everything off, per §6. Loops stop on completion, pause, error and off-screen.
18. RTL-safe CSS: logical properties only (`rtl-workspace.test.mjs`).
19. Every surface declares empty, loading, error and success states, each saying what to do next (`surface-states`, `ui-states`).

**App workspace**
20. The composer is hard-disabled before correct-place pairing, including shortcuts and Suggestions. Stop does not inherit the disabled state. History and connection help stay usable.
21. Unknown usage or cost shows "unavailable", never zero.
22. UI01-UI23 render only real run data. Large payloads are lazy.

**Performance and quality gates**
23. Landing payload stays inside `scripts/check-landing-budget.mjs` (20,000 B gzip markup+CSS, 36,000 B JS, 40,000 B images). The app entry graph stays inside `scripts/check-app-bundle.mjs`. `/ui-lab` and `/admin` stay in their own chunks.
24. No webfont, no canvas, no WebGL, and no images except SVG on the site. Below-fold sections use `content-visibility`.
25. `scripts/check-pixels.mjs` passes on 20 routes, 2 viewports and both themes, after a deliberate rebaseline.
26. Lighthouse, mobile profile, at least 90 in performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO, on every route. **I could not measure this.** It needs a tool the owner approves.
27. Also run `check-site-links.mjs`, `check-unstyled-classes.mjs` and the e2e specs under `tests/e2e/`.

## 13. Test and doc changes this requires

These must be rewritten with a recorded reason. Do not weaken or delete them.
- **`living-background.test.mjs`:** change the accent pin from `#5b7cfa` to `#ff8a4c`. Drop the `backdrop-filter: blur(24px)` composer pin, or re-scope it. Keep the same-product comparison and the bans on violet and gradients.
- **`glass-shell.test.mjs`** and **`glass.css`:** `glass.css` is retired, so rewrite the test for the new shell.
- **`picks-landing.test.mjs`, `animation-actually-wins.test.mjs`, `phone-drops-layers.test.mjs`:** rewrite for the retired canvas kit.
- **Contrast fixtures, `app-ink-ramp` and the `--nm-*` ramp:** re-derive from the new token values.
- **`contrast.test.mjs`:** add an assertion that accent text is used only with the correct per-theme token.
- **Docs:** record in `docs/DESIGN-LOCK.md`, `docs/DESIGN-TYPE.md` and `docs/autonomy/DECISIONS.md` that this spec supersedes graphite-plus-green, nothing-above-400, and D-GLASS-1.
- `AGENTS.md` records earlier site-test failures from the redesign in flight, so some pinned-copy and structure tests will go red. Rewrite those deliberately.
- **Pre-existing, not caused by this spec and not fixed by it:**
  - The 14 `check-unstyled-classes` findings.
  - The app entry chunk over its 150 kB budget. This spec must not add to it.
  - One failing web test (`cool_library_model`).
  - The stale `landing.spec.ts` e2e.

## 14. Constraint conflicts and open owner decisions

1. **Checklist and Lighthouse:** the owner defines the Lighthouse categories, device profile and URL set. Until then §12 item 26 is an assumption.
2. **Typeface and weight:** the owner confirms two overturns. The "no webfont" decision is kept, since the system stack stays. The "nothing above 400" rule is overturned, since this spec uses 500 and 600.
3. **Display-size cap:** this spec stays within the 3.5rem `check-copy` cap. No exception is needed.
4. **`/models`, `/proof`, `/changelog` and docs pages** that reference removed modes or tiers conflict with V3. The owner decides whether they stay. I changed no copy.
5. **Studs versus V3:** V3 says the site is not "an in-game studded HUD". The three-appearance cap is my mitigation. If the owner reads the Baseplate as too playful, the fallback is to keep only the logo studs, LED and loader, and drop the Baseplate.
6. **Ember next to warn and bad:** the separation relies on gold warn, rose bad and mandatory icons plus words. The owner should look at it on a real screen. A cooler accent would be safer for status but would look like the current site.
7. **Phones:** the Rail is only a thin progress bar there, so the Baseplate and the Snap carry the brand moment. This is weaker where many young creators are.
8. **Logo:** possible resemblance to a known mark (§8).
9. **Claude Design:** blocked until the owner runs `/design-login`.
10. **Cross-OS type:** the system stack renders differently per OS. Identity comes from the Rail, tracking, weight, tabular numerals and the logo, not the face.

## Gimmick and other behaviour (landing)
- **Layout shift:** `layout-shift` showed 0 entries at 320, 375, 640, 800 and 1280, on load and after placing bricks, on unthrottled localhost. At 320 and 375 placing a brick makes the page 52px taller when the bridge button appears. It fired within 500ms of the visitor's click, so it does not count toward CLS.
- **Baseplate:**
  - Every cell has a label and there is a polite live region. The live region said "Red brick placed at column 2, row 1".
  - The bridge wrote "A build 2 studs wide and up to 2 bricks high, 3 bricks in red." into the textarea. The URL did not change, so it never submitted.
  - Chips fill the textarea and do not submit.
  - Cells are at least 44px.
- **Grid size:** the visible grid is 9×5 at 1280, 12×5 at 800, 11×5 at 640, 6×4 at 375 and 5×4 at 320. The spec says 12×5 from 640px and 7×4 below. The implementer did not report this departure. The model is 12×5, but the view is narrower.
- **Snap:** the logo stud lifts on composer focus, and the transform is `none` under reduced motion.
- **Form method:** `form.composer` has `action="/app/signup"` and `method="get"`. The spec says it posts. With GET, the visitor's prompt would go into the URL.
- **JS weight:** 6 inline blocks of 17,228 B raw (about 4.6 KB gzip) plus the Baseplate script at 2,985 B gzip. The total is about 7.6 KB gzip.
- **Landing structure:** the spec's evidence strip and pricing teaser are absent, as the implementer said. The `01`/`02`/`03` ledger labels are present, and the Rail is real navigation.
- **Pointer spotlight:** the dashboard's pointer-following spotlight (`routes/dashboard.css:504`) is a banned pattern per the spec's motion section.

## Remaining gaps beyond the implementer's own list
These are findings the implementer did not mention.
- The app still has gradients and backdrop-filters on shell-adjacent routes.
- The app has infinite animations and font weights above 600.

- The workspace syntax-highlight colours fail contrast.
- Several landing links are shorter than 44px.
- The landing ships a raster image.
- The Baseplate grid is narrower than specified.
- The composer form uses GET.

I did not independently check the implementer's other disclosed gaps: the unbuilt site pages, the missing stud LED and loader, and the absent accent-text assertion.
